title: How the Hells Angels Work
summary: Josh and Chuck open with the April 2002 Laughlin, Nevada brawl at the Hair Is casino between the Mongols and the Hell's Angels, then trace the Hell's Angels motorcycle club from its founding in the Fontana/San Bernardino area of California (Burdue chapter, Otto Friedly) through the Oakland chapter led by Sonny Barger, their colors and patches, the membership process from hang-around to full patch, the World War Two bomber squadron myth, Hunter S. Thompson's time with the club, the Altamont free concert and Meredith Hunter's death, their 1970s meth trade, their international expansion, and a listener mail segment with corrections (Bernard Goetz, Clinkett pronunciation, Amish rumspringa).

segments.title: Opening banter and Laughlin casino brawl
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter, then Josh describes the April 2002 melee at the Hair Is casino in Laughlin, Nevada, between the Mongols and the Hell's Angels, which left two Hell's Angels and one Mongol dead. They note the Hell's Angels case ended mostly in plea bargains.

segments.title: Founding of the Hell's Angels
segments.summary: The first chapter, Burdue, began in the Fontana/San Bernardino area of California. Otto Friedly, formerly of another biker gang, is believed to have started it. Members later moved north to Oakland. The hosts discuss the World War Two bomber squadron myth and say the Hell's Angels website and research found only a loose name link to a pilot.
topics: Hell's Angels World War Two bomber squadron myth

segments.title: Oakland chapter and Sonny Barger
segments.summary: The Oakland chapter, founded in 1957, is credited with the club's growth, largely through Ralph Sonny Barger, who wrote successful books including an autobiography about the club.

segments.title: Colors, patches and the death head logo
segments.summary: The hosts describe the club's colors: red lettering on a white field, the top and bottom rockers, and the death head designed by San Francisco chapter president Frank Sedillo. The club is incorporated and guards its trademarks, suing Disney over the film Wild Hogs. Patches and the AFFA and 81 symbols are explained.

segments.title: Membership process and initiation
segments.summary: The hosts explain the path to membership: hang around, associate, prospect (no voting rights), then full patch member, which is for life. Requirements include owning a working motorcycle, a driver's license, and no police, prison guard, or child molester background. The hosts also discuss an unverified initiation story about feces and urine.

segments.title: Hunter S. Thompson and the Hell's Angels
segments.summary: Hunter S. Thompson wrote a 1960s article and then a book about the club after spending a year riding with them. Sonny Barger's view of him and the beating Thompson took from Hell's Angels, including Junkie George, are described. The book's gang rape claims are noted as allegations.

segments.title: Hippies, Ken Kesey, and Allen Ginsberg
segments.summary: Allen Ginsberg and Ken Kesey introduced Thompson to Barger, and the meeting helped make peace between the hippies and the Hell's Angels. Tom Wolfe's The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test is discussed, and the club's shared love of acid with the Merry Pranksters is mentioned.

segments.title: Altamont Speedway concert
segments.summary: The 1969 free concert at Altamont Speedway, where Hell's Angels were hired as security by the Rolling Stones, is described. Violence escalated, Marty Balin was knocked out, and the Grateful Dead left. Meredith Hunter was stabbed by Alan Passaro during the Stones' set, and Passaro was later acquitted. The Gimme Shelter film is recommended.

segments.title: Crime, meth trade, and international chapters
segments.summary: The hosts describe the club's 1970s dominance of methamphetamine, including a 1979 law enforcement estimate for the Burdue chapter, plus cocaine, heroin, and prostitution allegations. Sonny Barger served federal time. The club now has chapters in about 29 countries, including recent turf wars in Scandinavia and Australia, and George Harrison is said to have helped bring the club to England.

segments.title: Listener mail and corrections
segments.summary: Corrections include Bernard Goetz, who was wrongly called a serial killer, the pronunciation of Clinkett, and a listener's point that Amish teens on rumspringa may hear podcasts.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck thank listeners, point to HowStuffWorks search and the club's website, and sign off.
